## Exact hypotheses and remaining boundaries

**Parameter-uniform construction:** any commutative ring R, any q:R, and actual 2-by-2 matrices S=[[q,1],[0,-1]], T=[[-1,0],[3q,q]]. Each satisfies X²=(q−1)X+qI. Direct universal entry proofs give (ST)³=(TS)³=−q³I; associativity yields the six-factor braid. These are identities in arbitrary parameters, not sampled numerical checks. No inverse parameter is required for the identities; invertibility at arbitrary nonunit q is not asserted.

**Integer specialization:** q=1, coefficient ring integers. Both generators square to I; (ST)^6=I and (ST)^3≠I. These are exact kernel-proved specialization statements, not numerical evidence for a KL polynomial table, basis or faithful representation. No complete order or faithfulness theorem is asserted.

**Paper locators:** PDF page 2 supplies the Hecke algebra convention requiring correction; page 3 supplies the G2 example. Both exact PDF versions and their page-text hashes stay separate in JSON. The matrices are an assistant-proposed braid-six construction, not a claim that the printed G2 diagonal polynomial has been repaired or computed. K3 retains its earlier diagonal inconsistency check.

**Missing suppliers:** no universal Coxeter Hecke algebra, twelve-dimensional regular basis, Laurent-semilinear bar on this particular G2 module, general KL existence/uniqueness/degree theorem, recurrence, G2 polynomial table, affine/quantum variant or intersection-cohomology positivity is constructed. This two-dimensional braid-six matrix model is not the seven-dimensional exceptional algebraic-group representation required in E1. All seventeen unresolved specifications remain unchanged and version-bound. No historical influence, understanding date or reading event is inferred.

### Exact conclusion limits

The zeta-specific conclusion is **CONDITIONAL** on
\`rationalEventually\` and \`noEventuallySoficZero\`, proving
\`¬ RationalReal (z.im)\` *without* GRH. To conclude
\`¬ AlgebraicReal (z.im)\`, independently supply
\`algebraicOnLineEventually\` and
\`ZetaCriticalPlacement\` (the zeta critical-line component of
a correctly stated GRH, rather than GRH itself being proved).
No algebraic/rational ordinate has been shown to force soficity,
no actual zeta trace has been shown nonsofic, and no L-function
zero-height arithmetic theorem has been proved.
The 7/8 -> 3/4 half-plane interface still has an explicit
\`stageZeroFree\` premise at every refinement level; negligible
overhead does not construct those analytic estimates.

**Relationship classification:** LOCAL_IDENTITY_SOURCE_CANDIDATE
for finite graph, dynamic quotient and difference identities;
conditional graph/spectral and moment-preserving no-go interfaces;
finite symbolic full-shift FALSE-POSITIVE witness (not actual

## Case DYNAMIC-SOFIC-EXACT-LANGUAGE-20261023 — finite graph admission is not finite-state reconstruction

### Source identity and exact mathematical result

This is a **new repository-derived 2026 algebraic/information-theoretic source
candidate**, not an imported proof of a published sofic theorem. The source
credits mathematical direction to grwtsk contributors and formalization
assistance to OpenAI, while maintaining the original authorship of external
papers and imported source code. The precise source-of-truth note is
[`dynamic-sofic-exact-language-boundary.md`](dynamic-sofic-exact-language-boundary.md).

- `GRWTSK/NumberTheory/Farey/DynamicSoficExactLanguageBoundary.lean`,
  initial main integration [`fa9a047832ea4ae811323b468b3c53958e784e12`](https://github.com/grwtsk/math/commit/fa9a047832ea4ae811323b468b3c53958e784e12),
  Git blob `79d749e6d8ca99825df9e98305532454e0c446f1`.
- `GRWTSK/NumberTheory/Zeta/Riemann/BombieriDynamicSoficCoverBoundary.lean`,
  initial main integration [`f861e545096408ab1768f0c1ff438645efbfafbb`](https://github.com/grwtsk/math/commit/f861e545096408ab1768f0c1ff438645efbfafbb),
  Git blob `5e52e67b72a1f4d1ee214442114d7f452e2395e6`.
- Previously concurrent genuine dynamic/sofic source,
  `GRWTSK/NumberTheory/Farey/DynamicSoficSpectralCover.lean`,
  Git blob `8210e2055447ebbe482a7122d21ee09177c3b1c0`,
  and `GRWTSK/Logic/InformationLoss/DynamicPartitionRecovery.lean`,
  Git blob `e2f6170aabf05e3a6df8f6a67009d4a8ba913379`,
  remain intact. The latter already separates unrecoverable unanchored
  difference data from exact reconstruction using the initial anchor.

**Precise hypotheses and theorem claims.** A finite labeled graph has
a finite vertex type, an alphabet with a `Fintype` instance, an explicit
initial vertex, and an `edge : Vertex → Label → Vertex → Prop`
relation. An admitted word has an actual finite path. The one-vertex
graph allowing all labels admits **every prefix of every infinite
trace**, proving that **admissibility of a single trace is no
non-soficity obstruction**. The full-shift graph also accepts `[true]`,
which is not a prefix of the constant-false trace: graph admission and
*exact singleton-prefix-language recognition* differ.

The stronger predicate
`EventuallyExactPrefixPresented` requires **some** finite initial
shift and an actual graph that accepts precisely and only the finite
prefixes of the remaining trace. This is intentionally stronger than
mere graph-path admission and is **not** presented as a general
characterization of standard sofic subshifts or follower languages.

A `GrowingRefinement` consists of cells
`Fin (size n + 1)`, explicit source-to-stage maps, coarsening maps
between adjacent stages, a finite stage transition and two
commuting squares; it proves that an already distinguished pair cannot
merge at the next compatible refinement. A
`CommutingLosslessGraphCover` supplies a spectral lift with a total
left inverse, source/spectral step commutation, a graph projection and
actual path-label witnesses. Its spectral lift is injective and carries
every declared source readout, while a finite graph projection can
lose information. The typed `GrowingSoficSpectralDiagram` records
the partition-to-graph projection and obstructs decoding from a
colliding graph vertex. An
`AnalyticDynamicSoficPipeline` includes the already conditional
`ThreeQuarterRefinement` as a distinct field: zero-freeness to the
strict right of `3/4` still REQUIRES every stage estimate and the
cofinality premise, and cannot be generated by negligible overhead.

Finally the `OrdinateExactLanguageSuppliers` structure uses explicit
`HeightArithmetic` predicates, zero/critical-line predicates, a
height and labeled trace, and THREE **unsupplied** mathematical
assertions: rational height `→` eventual exact presentation,
algebraic critical-line height `→` eventual exact presentation,
and no eventual exact presentation for each selected trace. Given
these, irrationality follows **without GRH**. A separate predicate
`GRHFor` supplies critical-line placement and, **only in conjunction
with the two independent arithmetic/non-presentation premises**,
relative transcendence. GRH itself gives no transcendence.

### A. Rodgers--Tao heat-flow argument

**Paper.** Brad Rodgers and Terence Tao,
*The De Bruijn--Newman constant is non-negative*.
2018 preprint, arXiv:1801.05914; published 2020 in
*Forum of Mathematics, Pi* 8, e6.
Stable identifier: https://arxiv.org/abs/1801.05914.

**Exact external theorem/method and hypotheses.**
The paper studies the de Bruijn--Newman heat deformation `H_t` and proves
the complementary inequality `Lambda >= 0`. The proof assumes
`Lambda < 0` for contradiction and exploits the induced zero dynamics and
the resulting excessively rigid local equilibrium, contradicting known zeta
zero statistics. GRWTSK does **not** import this theorem, the PDE/ODE system,
or the zero-statistics estimates. The paper supplies only the methodological
pattern: a dynamically evolving zero-bearing process plus a contradiction from
information/rigidity constraints.

### B. Huffman minimum-redundancy coding

### C. Bombieri's Weil functional and RH survey

**Paper 1.** Enrico Bombieri,

**Exact external theorem/method and hypotheses.**
Bombieri's memoir studies Weil's explicit formula and its associated quadratic
functional; the full functional is positive semidefinite iff RH, under the
paper's test-function framework. The GRWTSK formalization does **not** import
that full equivalence. It extracts the ordinary and reciprocal moment data on
a deliberately finite canonical square-tent coefficient source, then proves an
exact collision in that reduced observation.

### D. OpenAI quasi-Riemann hypothesis

**Paper.** OpenAI,
*The Quasi-Riemann Hypothesis: A Zero-Free Half-Plane Re(s)>7/8*,
OpenAI Math Release preprint, 30 September 2026.
Stable release identifier:
`OAI:The-Quasi-Riemann-Hypothesis-September-30-2026`.
Stable source:
https://github.com/openai/math/blob/main/preprints/The-Quasi-Riemann-Hypothesis-September-30-2026/paper.pdf.

**Exact external theorem and hypotheses.**
The accompanying formalization states the fixed zero-free half-plane
`Re(s)>7/8` for the Riemann zeta function and uniformly for Dirichlet
L-functions; the release also records the finite-order Hecke
`Q(sqrt(-3))` case. Principal-character poles at one are excluded in the
corresponding L-function statements. GRWTSK currently does not import that Lean
theorem into the dynamic program; it records `7/8` as a supplied analytic
seed and requires every later refinement stage independently.

### E. Sofic shifts, labeled graph languages, and finite continuation contexts

**Paper 1.** Benjamin Weiss,
*Subshifts of finite type and sofic systems*,
*Monatshefte fuer Mathematik* 77 (1973), 462--474.
DOI: https://doi.org/10.1007/BF01295322.

**Paper 2.** Nataša Jonoska,
*Sofic shifts with synchronizing presentations*,
*Theoretical Computer Science* 158 (1996), 81--115.
DOI: https://doi.org/10.1016/0304-3975(96)00058-8.

**Paper 3.** Justin Cai and Rafael Frongillo,
*Computational complexity of problems for deterministic presentations of
sofic shifts*, *Theoretical Computer Science* 936 (2022), 92--115.
DOI: https://doi.org/10.1016/j.tcs.2022.09.017;
arXiv:2112.03484.

**Exact external method and hypotheses.**
These sources use finite labeled directed graphs and their finite-word
languages to present sofic systems; the later literature emphasizes the
automata/regular-language viewpoint and exact language equality rather than
mere readability of a single path. GRWTSK does not import a published
classification theorem. It freshly proves the finite graph/path identities and
a finite right-context bound: continuation behavior of a word is determined by
its finite set of reachable end states. Consequently, arbitrarily many
pairwise continuation-distinguishable contexts obstruct every exact finite
graph presentation.

### A. Rodgers–Tao heat deformation: primary-source locators now checked

**Title, byline, edition and permanent links:** Brad Rodgers and
Terence Tao, *The de Bruijn–Newman constant is non-negative*,
arXiv preprint dated **18 January 2018**, arXiv:1801.05914;
published *Forum of Mathematics, Pi* **8 (2020), e6**, DOI
[10.1017/fmp.2020.6](https://doi.org/10.1017/fmp.2020.6).
Reviewed primary published source:
[Cambridge 2020 PDF](https://www.cambridge.org/core/services/aop-cambridge-core/content/view/D4B85BA067E2D5A71D87E4FFB0D21E46/S2050508620000062a.pdf/de_bruijnnewman_constant_is_nonnegative.pdf).

**Verified exact locators and hypotheses:**
printed **p. 2, §1, equation (1)** defines
\`H₀(z)=(1/8) ξ(1/2+i z/2)\`; **p. 2, equation (4)**
defines \`H_t(z)=∫₀^∞ exp(t u²) Φ(u) cos(zu) du\`
for real \`t\` and the explicit super-exponentially decaying
theta kernel \`Φ\` (equation (3)). The source identifies the
**backward** heat equation \`∂_t H_t=-∂²_z H_t\`.
**Printed p. 3, Theorem 1** concludes \`Λ≥0\`; its proof
uses the contrary \`Λ<0\`, the zero dynamics and local-equilibrium
contradiction (see §1 pp. 4–6; equation (5) on printed p. 5).
These are *external published analytic statements*, **not imported
Lean results**. No passage claims Huffman decoding, finite soficity,
irrational or transcendental zero ordinates.

fully qualified namespaces**:

### C. Bombieri's precise Weil-class two moments: printed page located

**Author/title/version:** Enrico Bombieri, *Problems of the
Millennium: the Riemann Hypothesis*, Clay Mathematics Institute
official problem description, **2000**. Stable original PDF:
[claymath.org/wp-content/uploads/2022/05/riemann.pdf](https://www.claymath.org/wp-content/uploads/2022/05/riemann.pdf).
The **2022 URL upload is not the publication year**.

**Verified exact method and assumptions:** printed **p. 8,
§V, “Further evidence: the explicit formula”** defines the
test-function class \`W\` of (piecewise) continuously
differentiable complex functions on \`(0,∞)\` with specified
one-sided/average-value conventions and
\`f(x)=O(x^δ)\` at zero and \`O(x^(-1-δ))\` at infinity
for some \`δ>0\`; the explicit formula uses
\`f̃(s)=∫₀^∞ f(x)x^s dx/x\`.
**Printed p. 9, §V, paragraph after the explicit formula**
attributes to Weil the RH-equivalent **negativity** of the
specified explicit-formula right-hand side for
\`f(x)=∫₀^∞ g(xy) conj(g(y))dy\`, with \`g∈W\`
satisfying **both distinct conditions**
\`∫₀^∞g(x)dx/x=0\` and \`∫₀^∞g(x)dx=0\`.
Those are the exact source **moment constraints**.
The local moment pair is **not** an equivalent replacement for
the whole Guinand–Weil quadratic form or the full test class.

## Case EXACT-DYNAMIC-SOFIC-COVER-VALIDATION-20261023

**Source identities and classification.** Local 2026 formalization, local attribution
`grwtsk contributors`. Published method background:
John Myhill (1957), *Finite Automata and the Representation of Events*, WADC
Technical Report 57-624, pp. 112–137 ([catalog entry](https://cir.nii.ac.jp/crid/1570854176000165888?lang=en));
Anil Nerode (1958), *Linear Automaton Transformations*, Proceedings of the AMS
9(4), pp. 541–544 ([DOI 10.1090/S0002-9939-1958-0135681-9](https://doi.org/10.1090/S0002-9939-1958-0135681-9)).
Exact local method: a finite labeled graph's right continuation behavior is
determined by its finite subset of reachable endpoints. Arbitrarily many
pairwise distinguishable right contexts refute an exact finite-state language
presentation. This is a locally proved one-way analogue, not a kernel import
of the full published Myhill–Nerode theorem, its converse, minimization algorithm,
or a bi-infinite sofic-shift theorem. Existing heat-flow/Huffman/QRH context
remains methodological background under the companion
[dynamic cover provenance record](dynamic-sofic-spectral-cover.md); no analytic
heat flow, zero-free theorem or historical influence is inferred.

## Case ZETA-SPECTRAL-BOMBIERI-DYNAMIC-VALIDATION-20261023

**Titles, byline and version.** *Actual zeta base problem for conditional
RH-to-generalized spectral transport* and *Bombieri two-moment fibers obstruct
every moment-only dynamic refinement*, local 2026 formalizations by
`grwtsk contributors`, version
[math@801a9d410e69c8bedc59096f22dae0cfd770d876](https://github.com/grwtsk/math/commit/801a9d410e69c8bedc59096f22dae0cfd770d876).
This is a fresh qualification of the exact source below. Earlier source-only
comments, passive requests and pre-redaction hashes remain historical; they do
not certify these bytes. No Noe execution, external replay or analytic-premise
discharge is claimed by this local verification.

**Published context and exact method.** Enrico Bombieri, *Problems of the
Millennium: the Riemann Hypothesis* (2000), official
[Clay problem description](https://www.claymath.org/wp-content/uploads/2022/05/riemann.pdf),
§V, printed pp. 8–9: the source test class has regularity and decay conditions,
and the Weil criterion cited there requires BOTH ordinary and reciprocal
zero moments. The local method uses the exact pair of moments on the
stage-two/three/four canonical square-tent coefficient space. It does not
replace the classical Guinand–Weil form or its test-class hypotheses by that pair.
David A. Huffman, *A Method for the Construction of Minimum-Redundancy Codes*,
Proceedings of the IRE 40(9), 1098–1101 (1952),
[DOI 10.1109/JRPROC.1952.273898](https://doi.org/10.1109/JRPROC.1952.273898),
is finite-alphabet coding background. The local imported byte-packet round trip
is checked here; the paper's minimum-expected-length theorem is not imported
or proved. The existing finite-automata/sofic-language bibliography remains
method background. No historical influence or literal heat-flow/codec identity
is inferred from a method match.

**Spectral transport.** Namespace
`GRWTSK.RiemannHypothesis.ZetaSpectralGRHBridge`:
`zetaZeroProblem` uses `ActualZetaZero` and exactly `z.re = 1/2`;
`zetaZeroProblem_hypothesis_iff` identifies its hypothesis with
`ZetaCriticalPlacement`. The checked
`zetaCriticalPlacement_implies_generalized_of_spectralCovers` requires a supplied
`SpectralCoverFamily` from that actual zeta problem.
`generalized_implies_zetaCriticalPlacement_of_member_specialization` requires an
actual family member and `BaseSpecialization` preserving zeros and reflecting
criticality. The equivalence

## Case BSZ-01 — finite prime-dilation bookkeeping (2026-10-23)

**Primary methodological reference:** Jean Bourgain, Peter Sarnak, Tamar Ziegler,
*Disjointness of Mobius from horocycle flows* (2011), arXiv:1110.0992v1,
https://arxiv.org/abs/1110.0992. Method locator: Theorem 2 and §2.

uniform small correlations for distinct primes in a specified range, and
sufficiently large summation length. Its quantitative bound has scale

**New deduced paper-dependent obstruction, not yet encoded as a Lean declaration:** For fixed irrational `α` and `λ ≠ 0`, the bounded self-adjoint almost Mathieu operator satisfies `‖H‖≤2+2|λ|`, and its spectrum lies in a finite interval. Distinct labels `{nα}`, `n∈ℤ\{0}`, are distinct modulo one; Dry Ten Martini provides different nonempty open bounded spectral gaps `(a_n,b_n)` for all such labels. Their interiors are disjoint, so for every `ε>0` at most finitely many have width `b_n-a_n≥ε` (otherwise sufficiently many disjoint ε-wide intervals would exceed the total enclosing spectral interval). Therefore `b_n-a_n→0` as `|n|→∞`. For midpoint `E_n=(a_n+b_n)/2`, the full-gap midpoint distance is `d_n=(b_n-a_n)/2`, and the self-adjoint spectral-theorem inequality `‖(H-E_n)x‖² ≥ d_n²‖x‖²` applies on the **operator domain** (for bounded H, all of Hilbert space); its `d_n²` is not uniformly positive in `n`. This is **not** a claim that all Yang--Mills lifting constants vanish, only that uniform physical mass cannot be deduced merely by taking the minimum of these infinitely many labeled-gap widths. The width theorem is a new mathematical proof argument to formalize, not an asserted source theorem of Avila or Borgnia--Faust and not a successful Lean compilation.

**Physically meaningful conditional return criterion (unproved premises, YM-B only if connected to a genuine reconstructed physical Hamiltonian):** Let `q_{a,L}` be the nonnegative closed quadratic form of the appropriately normalized physical gauge-invariant Hamiltonian on its *vacuum-orthogonal* Hilbert space, decomposed in its form domain as `u+v` into a lifted closed sector and an orthogonal complement. Then `q_{a,L}[u+v]≥(min(m_M,m_C)-c)‖u+v‖²`. Physical conclusion further requires actual `H_{a,L}` construction, vacuum compatibility, domain-preserving orthogonal projection, correct physical energy normalization, gauge invariance, and a rigorous continuum reconstruction/limit theorem. These premises are **not** furnished by the almost Mathieu theorem or by abstract sector decomposition. An auxiliary `(H-E)^2` is not itself the physical Yang--Mills Hamiltonian.

### Case DRY-TEN-MARTINI-FERMI-PROJECTIVE-YM-20261025: exact conditional algebraic bridge to noncommutative gauge geometry

**Mathematical status:** explicit algebraic proof argument / future Lean theorem target; **no new local Lean source, no independently checked upstream Lean theorem, no native compilation, no fresh kernel checking, and no transitive axiom audit**. This is a follow-up to Case DRY-TEN-MARTINI-YM-SPECTRAL-LIFT-20261025 and GitHub verification issue [#1291](https://github.com/grwtsk/math/issues/1291). Attribution for this local deduction: **grwtsk contributors**; upstream source: Alain Connes and Marc A. Rieffel, *Yang–Mills for Non-commutative Two-Tori* (1987), https://math.berkeley.edu/~rieffel/papers/yang_mills.pdf; the smooth noncommutative-torus setting is the source of the geometric *definitions*, but this specific lifted-Harper coercivity is a new mathematical deduction rather than a theorem ascribed to that article.

**Exact conditional lifting theorem to formalize, YM-D structural:** Assume (a) irrational rotation unital C*-algebra `A_α` and a dense smooth *-subalgebra `A_α^∞` with commuting *-derivations `δ₁,δ₂`; (b) a bounded self-adjoint Harper element `h=U+U*+λ(V+V*)∈A_α^∞` with `UV=e^{2πiα}VU`; (c) `E∈ℝ\σ_A(h)` with `d=dist(E,σ_A(h))>0`; (d) the spectral/Riesz projection `p=1_{(-∞,E)}(h)` belongs to `A_α^∞` (for example via spectral invariance under holomorphic functional calculus). Then:

1. `p=p*=p²` and `ph=hp`; `𝓔=pA_α^∞` is a finitely generated projective right module, with right A-valued inner product `⟨pa,pb⟩_A=a*pb`.
2. Self-adjoint functional calculus gives the positive element `(h-E)^2-d² 1≥0` in `A_α`. Left multiplication by `(h-E)^2` preserves `𝓔` since it commutes with p, and for all `s=pa`, `⟨s,(h-E)^2s⟩_A-d²⟨s,s⟩_A=a* p((h-E)^2-d²1)p a≥0`. This is **true projective-module spectral coercivity** (source lifting), but not curvature or physical Hamiltonian coercivity.
3. Grassmann connections `∇ᵢ(s)=p δᵢ(s)` obey the right-module Leibniz identity `∇ᵢ(sa)=∇ᵢ(s)a+sδᵢ(a)`; with commuting derivations, their curvature obeys `[∇₁,∇₂]s=p[δ₁p,δ₂p]p s`. The identity follows from `pδᵢ(p)p=0` obtained by differentiating `p²=p`.
4. With an appropriate faithful positive trace `τ` on A (e.g. canonical trace), the gauge-theoretic quadratic expression `YM(∇)=τ(F_{12}*F_{12})≥0` is invariant under unitary endomorphism gauge conjugacy `F↦gFg*`; retain the paper's chosen sign, coupling and trace normalization when connecting to its functional. This is a noncommutative **two-torus** action, not the 4D pure quantum Yang--Mills action.

The positive `YM(∇)` expression **does not follow to be bounded below by d²**, and the positive endomorphism `(h-E)^2` is **not** the Yang--Mills Hamiltonian.
